criteria.criterion: docs/spec.toml entry OLY-B-S3-01 no longer has mechanism = "none"; its mechanism names crates/athena-core/src/lab.rs, owner stays "Athena", and its measure ends with `status: not shown` and names the test file crates/athena-core/tests/lab_runs.rs.
criteria.evidence: Read docs/spec.toml lines 2961-2964. The mechanism is "LabConfig::parse, LabConfig::check_run and LabConfig::fingerprint in crates/athena-core/src/lab.rs: ...". The owner is "Athena". The measure is "crates/athena-core/tests/lab_runs.rs parses valid and invalid configurations ... status: not shown". The diff touches only this entry.

criteria.criterion: crates/athena-core/src/lab.rs exists, is exported from crates/athena-core/src/lib.rs, and defines a lab configuration with the three systems, a task, a pinned commit and a spend cap in USD per system, plus a fingerprint of the configuration.
criteria.evidence: Read in the diff. lab.rs defines `SYSTEMS = ["athena","firstmate","hermes"]` and `LabConfig { task, commit, caps_usd: BTreeMap<String,f64> }`, with `parse`, `check_run` and `fingerprint`. lib.rs adds `pub mod lab;` and a doc bullet for it. The test target imports `athena_core::lab::{LabConfig, LabError}` and compiles.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core --test lab_runs`: a valid config with three systems and positive caps is accepted; configs missing a system, with a zero or negative cap, or without a pinned commit are refused; a run whose recorded spend reaches its cap is refused; the same config gives the same fingerprint and a changed cap gives a different one.
criteria.evidence: I ran the command and all 7 tests passed: a_valid_config_is_accepted, a_missing_system_is_refused (MissingSystem("hermes")), a_zero_or_negative_cap_is_refused (0.0 and -1.0 give BadCap), a_missing_or_unpinned_commit_is_refused (no commit line and commit="main" give NoCommit), a_run_at_its_cap_is_refused (4.99 is allowed, 5.0 is refused, 9.0 against a 2.5 cap is refused), the_fingerprint_follows_the_configuration (same config gives the same fingerprint; changing athena's cap 5.0 to 6.0 changes it), and spec_entry_has_a_real_mechanism.

criteria.criterion: The test lab_runs.rs also reads docs/spec.toml and fails if the OLY-B-S3-01 entry has mechanism none, no owner, or a measure not ending in a status label; it fails when lab.rs's validation is removed and passes with it.
criteria.evidence: spec_entry_has_a_real_mechanism reads ../../docs/spec.toml and takes the text from `id = "OLY-B-S3-01"` up to the next `[[requirement]]` (a `[[requirement.source]]` header does not match that string). It asserts there is no `mechanism = "none"`, that lab.rs is named, that `owner = "Athena"` is present, and that the measure ends `status: not shown` and names lab_runs.rs. That test passed. `git show HEAD~1:crates/athena-core/src/lib.rs` shows the base has no `pub mod lab`, so lab_runs.rs cannot compile, and therefore fails, without the mechanism. The refusal tests use unwrap_err() and assert exact errors, so a parse with its validation removed would make them fail. This last point is from reading the code: I did not edit the tree to try it, because my role forbids changes.

findings.summary: A file outside the expected deliverables changed: xtask/shard-timings.txt
findings.evidence: xtask/shard-timings.txt is not on the deliverables list, but the diff adds `athena-core --test lab_runs 5.00` to it. docs/decisions.md (around line 4339) has a rule that every test target must have a line in this file, so the edit is needed. It is still outside the stated scope. Cargo.toml was on the list but did not need to change.

findings.summary: check_run allows a run when the recorded spend is NaN or negative
findings.evidence: The refusal is `if spent_usd >= cap`. With a NaN spend the comparison is false, so check_run returns Ok and the cap is bypassed. A negative spend is also accepted. Simpler and safer: refuse unless `spent_usd.is_finite() && spent_usd >= 0.0 && spent_usd < cap`, and add a test for it.

findings.summary: The fingerprint uses hand-written FNV-1a although sha2 is already a workspace dependency
findings.evidence: The root Cargo.toml line 48 declares `sha2 = "0.10"`, and athena-data, athena-git and xtask already use it. The reading's buy-first assumption said to reuse a hash crate from Cargo.lock if one exists. A 64-bit non-cryptographic hash works as an identifier but is weaker as a reproducibility key. The alternative is to add `sha2.workspace = true` to athena-core (Cargo.toml was already a deliverable) and hash the same canonical string.

findings.summary: No test covers the UnknownSystem error
findings.evidence: No test passes an extra key under [caps_usd], or an unknown system to check_run, so the UnknownSystem branch has no test.

summary: The change does what the accepted reading asked, and I recommend a pass. It adds crates/athena-core/src/lab.rs, which reads a lab configuration and refuses it without a task, a pinned 40-hex commit, or a positive USD cap for each of athena, firstmate and hermes. It also refuses a run once its recorded spend reaches the cap, and gives each configuration an FNV-1a fingerprint. The module is exported from lib.rs. The OLY-B-S3-01 entry in docs/spec.toml now names lab.rs as its mechanism, keeps owner Athena, and has a measure that names the test file and ends `status: not shown`. CHANGELOG.md has a matching entry. I ran `cargo test -p athena-core --test lab_runs`, and all 7 tests passed. The base commit has no `pub mod lab`, so the test file cannot compile without the mechanism. fmt, clippy and the full test suite passed in the CI checks Athena recorded for this commit. I found four minor problems and nothing blocking: xtask/shard-timings.txt changed although it is not on the deliverables list (a repo rule requires it); check_run allows a run when the spend is NaN or negative; the fingerprint uses hand-written FNV-1a although sha2 is already a workspace dependency, which the reading's buy-first assumption preferred; and no test covers the UnknownSystem error.
